name: Liposomal IGF-1

lead: Liposomal IGF-1 is a topical idea for thicker scalp hair: deliver the growth factor IGF-1 to hair follicles inside fat-like carriers.

IGF-1 is made naturally by follicle cells, and a 2025 review reports that it stimulates follicle proliferation and blood vessel growth and extends the growth phase through PI3K/Akt and MAPK/ERK signalling. The supporting work is laboratory and animal research; no human hair-loss trial of a topical liposomal form was found.

paras: It is discussed in hair-loss communities as a scalp product applied topically, often next to established hair treatments. Hair changes are generally judged over several months.
Safety of topical IGF-1 on the scalp has not been established in published trials. It is an unapproved product for hair.

angle.text: Liposomal IGF-1 is meant to carry IGF-1 to the follicle, extend the growth phase and give thicker scalp hair. In lab work IGF-1 promotes follicle proliferation; human trials of the topical form have not been found.

lead: Liposomal IGF-1 refers to insulin-like growth factor 1 packaged in liposomes for topical application to the scalp. IGF-1 is a growth factor made mainly by dermal papilla cells in hair-bearing skin; a 2025 review reports that it stimulates follicle proliferation and vascularization and promotes the growth (anagen) phase through PI3K/Akt and MAPK/ERK signalling. [1]
Community interest rests largely on animal and laboratory work. No clinical trial of a liposomal topical IGF-1 for hair loss appears among the sources reviewed.

paras: The 2025 review describes IGF-1 as inhibiting apoptosis, prolonging the follicular growth phase and increasing VEGF expression, which supports microcirculation around the follicle. [1]

Topical IGF-1 has been tested outside hair: a randomized trial in the middle ear used IGF-1-impregnated gelatin hydrogels for sudden deafness refractory to corticosteroids. That work concerns hearing, not hair, and is not evidence about scalp use. [2][3]
No studies found. Mechanistic and preclinical literature on IGF-1 in hair regeneration exists, [1] but no human trial of a liposomal scalp product was located.
